The file `decorators.py` defines a custom decorator `has_team_required`, which is used to ensure that the user has a team. The user has one team if they satisfy one of two conditions:

1. They belong to exactly one team.
2. They are a member of the staff.

The condition `u.team_set.all().count() == 1` checks if the user belongs to exactly one team, and if they are staff, the check is skipped. This condition allows users with more than one team to quit a team, as they no longer fall under the checked-condition.

If you call the delete-view as an unauthenticated user, you will get a "HTTP 404: Not Found"-error, because Django tries to load the object (the team), which you don't have permission to see.

If you want a "403: Forbidden" when doing this, you can use Django's `permission_required`-decorator, e.g.:

```python
@permission_required('hackingweek.delete_team', raise_exception=True)
@login_required
def quit_team(request, team_id):
    ...
```

Note that the `login_required`-decorator can be omitted in this case.
